# S173 — Role matrix editor, wire half: relay-roles write verbs and matrix.edit

ork can change the role matrix through slicer: five `slicer relay-roles` write verbs in the slicer client, a daemon method `matrix.edit` that previews or runs one of them in the registered project, and the client call. No TUI and no CLI command; the TUI editor is the next slice (`matrix-editor-tui`).

## Why

S173 (role matrix editor) was sized L and carries its own note to split into wire and TUI halves. This is the wire half; the TUI half is a new item that depends on it (owner, 2026-10-31: split S173; agent, vendor and model are free text, with a warning when ork has no adapter for the agent). The other three opens were answered on 2026-10-29 (S173 note): TUI only (no `ork roles matrix set` command), the five verbs `add`, `set`, `remove`, `move` and `rule-edit`, and edits left uncommitted. S168, the read-only view, is done.

Facts re-checked at HEAD (2026-10-31):
- The matrix is slicer's: `.slicer/relay-roles.json`, changed only through `slicer relay-roles add|set|remove|move|rule-add|rule-edit|rule-remove` (`slicer relay-roles --help`); each takes `--render`, `--json`, `--strict`. ork calls only `relay-roles show --json` (`internal/slicercli/write.go:222-230`, `RelayMatrix`) and `recommend` (`write.go:107`, `RecommendRoles`). Owner decision `lineup.source` (`docs/boundaries.md:14`).
- Flags (from `slicer relay-roles add|set|remove|move|rule-edit --help`): `add` needs `--role` (implementer, reviewer, gate, architect or orchestrator) and takes `--size --effort --importance --urgency --well-specified --split --sliver --agent --vendor --model --reasoning --note`; `set ID` takes the same flags, each optional; `remove ID`; `move ID [--before ID | --last]`; `rule-edit ID TEXT` (two positionals). `add` and `set` print the row as JSON (an `id` key); `set` with `--model=` clears the field (tried in a scratch project on 2026-10-31). An unknown row id exits 2 with `{"error":{"code":"unknown_role_row",...}}`.
- Slicer's parser is argparse, which reads a value that starts with `-` and has no space as an option: `set r1 --model -x` is refused and `--model=-x` is accepted (tried in a scratch project, 2026-10-31). Every value is therefore passed attached (`--model=VALUE`). `rule-edit` takes its text as a positional, and `Client.write` appends `--root ROOT` after the arguments (`write.go:117-124`), so the `--` separator cannot be used; the verb refuses a dash-leading text that has no space.
- `internal/daemon/matrix.go` exists (S168): `rolesMatrix`, `MatrixRow{ID, Role, Agent, Use}` and `matrixUse`. `matrixAdapters` (`internal/daemon/runs.go:336-337`) maps the matrix `agent` to an adapter: `claude code` to `claude`, `codex` to `codex` (adj 155). A row whose agent is not in that map is skipped when a plan is built (`runs.go:417,436`).
- The pattern for a slicer write with no run record is `item.note`: `internal/daemon/items.go:34-49` calls `d.runDeps(proj).Slicer.Note(ctx, runrec.Writer{}, proj.Path, ...)`; a zero `Writer` logs nothing and retries a `locked` exit with its backoff (`internal/runrec/writer.go:63-80`). The write runs in the project's main checkout and leaves the change uncommitted.
- A run already started keeps its lineup (`runrec.Record.Lineup`). A launch plan that an edit changes is refused by the `plan changed` check at `run.start`; nothing in this slice touches it.

New wire (all *proposed*, extending the shape the S173 note already named, `matrix.edit {project, op, id, fields}`):
- `matrix.edit` params `{project, op, id?, fields?, before?, last?, text?, preview?}`. `op` is `add`, `set`, `remove`, `move` or `rule-edit`. `fields` is a map from flag name to text value for `add` and `set`: a name that is absent is not passed; a name with an empty value clears that field. The allowed names are `role size effort importance urgency well-specified split sliver agent vendor model reasoning note`. Free text for agent, vendor and model; ork does not check them (slicer's validation errors come back verbatim).
- Result `{command, warning?, id?, done}`. `command` is the line the owner confirms: `slicer relay-roles` plus the arguments, with `--render` and without `--json` or `--root`, values quoted for a shell when they hold anything but letters, digits and `_@%+=:,./-`. `preview: true` returns it without running anything (`done` false). `warning` is set when `fields.agent` is given and no adapter matches (`matrixAdapters`, lower-cased): `agent "X" has no ork adapter: a plan skips this row`. `id` is the new row's id after `add`.
- `roles.matrix` rows also carry `vendor`, `model`, `reasoning` and `note` (omitted when empty) so that the editor can show and prefill a row.

## Failing tests

Slicer client, `internal/slicercli/write_test.go` (use `client(t, clitest.Route{...})`; routes match exact argv):
- `TestRelayRowSetPassesOnlyTheGivenFields`: `RelayRowSet(ctx, w, root, "r5", RowFields{"model": "opus"})` runs exactly `relay-roles set r5 --model=opus --render --json --root ROOT`.
- `TestRelayRowFieldsAreAttachedAndSorted`: `{"note": "-x", "model": "", "agent": "Codex"}` gives `--agent=Codex --model= --note=-x` in that order (sorted by name).
- `TestRelayRowAddRemoveMoveRuleEditArgv`: the argv of `add` (`relay-roles add --role=reviewer --agent=Codex --render --json`), `remove r5`, `move r5 --before=r2`, `move r5 --last`, and `rule-edit u3 TEXT` with TEXT after the id and before `--render`.
- `TestRelayRowAddReturnsTheNewID`: stdout `{"id":"r17","role":"reviewer"}` gives `"r17"`; stdout without an id is an error.
- `TestRelayRowRefusalsMakeNoCall`: empty or blank id; `add` without a `role`; `set` with no fields; `move` with both or neither of before and last; a field name outside the allowed list; `rule-edit` with blank text, or text that starts with `-` and has no space (`"-x"`; but `"- x"` is allowed). Each returns an error and the fake records no call.
Fails first: none of these functions exist.

Daemon, `internal/daemon/matrix_test.go` (use `readDaemon`, `request`, `waveRoot` and `clitest.Route{Prefix: true}` as the neighbouring tests do):
- `TestMatrixEditRunsTheSlicerCommand`: `matrix.edit {"project":"p","op":"set","id":"r5","fields":{"model":"opus"}}` makes exactly one slicer call, `relay-roles set r5 --model=opus --render --json --root <path>`, and returns `{command: "slicer relay-roles set r5 --model=opus --render", done: true}`; no run record is created.
- `TestMatrixEditPreviewRunsNothing`: the same with `preview: true` returns the same `command`, `done` false and no slicer call.
- `TestMatrixEditPassesSlicersRefusalThrough`: a failing `relay-roles set` (exit 2, `{"error":{"code":"unknown_role_row","message":"no such relay role row: r99"}}`) returns that code and message unchanged.
- `TestMatrixEditRefusesAnUnregisteredProject`: `not_found`, no slicer call.
- `TestMatrixEditRefusesBadRequests`: missing project, unknown op, missing id for `set|remove|move|rule-edit`, `add` without `fields.role`, `set` without fields, `move` with both or neither of `before` and `last`, a field name outside the list, `fields` on `remove`, blank `text`: each is `bad_params` and makes no call.
- `TestMatrixEditWarnsOnAnAgentWithoutAnAdapter`: `fields.agent` `Acme Agent` sets `warning`; `Claude Code`, `codex` and `Codex` do not; a `set` without an agent field never warns. The edit still runs.
- `TestMatrixEditAddReturnsTheNewRowID`: `add` with stdout `{"id":"r17"}` returns `id` `r17`.
- `TestMatrixEditQuotesValuesInTheCommand`: a note `two words` shows as `--note='two words'` in `command`, while the argv sent to slicer has the raw `--note=two words`.
- `TestRolesMatrixRowsCarryVendorModelReasoningAndNote`: `roles.matrix` rows include `vendor`, `model`, `reasoning`, and `note` when non-empty (extend `matrixShow` with a note on one row).
- `TestMatrixEditOverTheSocket`: the client call returns the result and slicer's error code as the wire carries them (like `TestRolesMatrixOverTheSocket`).
Fails first: no `matrix.edit` method, no row fields.

Argument order (re-anchored by the implementer): fields go in name order with role first, so the add argv above (`--role=reviewer --agent=Codex`) and the sorted-order test (`--agent --model --note`) both hold. RowArgs is the exported argv builder the daemon uses for its command line.
